title: Doorstep: caretaking alerts from a parent's Ring doorbell

lines.text: Ada lives two hundred miles from her mum, Grace.
At five o'clock, Doorstep tells her a parcel has sat on Grace's front step for hours,
shows her the Ring camera's picture, and explains exactly why.
Doorbell cameras give families clips and a stream of pings.
But not the answer to the one question that matters: is Mum's day normal?
Doorstep watches the timing and the absences, and stays quiet when everything fits.
Here's an example day at sixty times speed.
Every Ring event becomes one plain sentence, written by Amazon Bedrock's Nova Lite.
It describes what happens, and never identifies anyone.
The carer is due between nine and half past ten.
When nobody comes, a rules engine, not AI, raises one gentle alert,
and explains why, in terms of Grace's care plan.
From the alert, Ada can call her mum or the carer,
be reminded in half an hour, or, if the visit was moved, mark it as expected.
Everything is kept in the alert's history.
At the end of the day, Nova Lite writes Ada a short note:
Mum's day, in a few sentences.
For Grace, who doesn't always hear the chime, a big-screen visual doorbell.
Late at night, someone rings, and the TV says what's happening at the door, in words.
One press of OK dismisses it.
It's built on the real Ring Partner API: devices, event history, snapshots and live view.
Captions and digests come from Amazon Bedrock, cached so nothing is paid for twice.
Example days are labelled honestly. Nothing pretends.
Doorstep.
Peace of mind that's quiet when everything's fine.
